facts.fact: MediaPipe FaceMesh detects 468 face landmarks in real time (per search-result summaries of the MediaPipe Face Mesh documentation and a DEV Community article).
With refined landmarks enabled, MediaPipe Face Mesh outputs 478 landmarks per face; the refinement uses an attention mesh model to refine coordinates around eyes and lips and adds iris landmarks.

mozi1924/mediapipe-facecap-for-blender is a MediaPipe-based face capture project with a companion Blender add-on ('receiver') and a transmitter program; it is not an add-on literally named 'FaceMesh Capture'.

Faceit (Superhive, formerly Blender Market) is a paid add-on that semi-automatically generates facial shape keys, with ARKit-style, Audio2Face, tongue and phoneme presets, and a bake step that converts modifier-stack, pose and sculpt deformation into shape keys.
Faceit's listing states Blender compatibility 3.0 to 5.2.

Face Shape Key Rig is a free GPL add-on on Blender Extensions that builds in-viewport sliders and 2D pads driven by bones and drivers to animate existing shape keys; it supports iFacialMocap capture and audio lipsync. Its GitHub page states it requires Blender 5.2 or newer.
Face Shape Key Rig controls existing shape keys; it does not generate them. Faceit is the comparable tool that creates shape keys.

CaptureForge (H0wZy/captureforge) is a GPL-3.0 Blender extension suite that converts a posed face rig to ARKit 52 blendshapes and drives them from video or webcam, without an iPhone; it also lists a quality inspector and auto face rig features.
MPFB2 (MakeHuman Community Plugin for Blender) code is GPL v3 or later, per the Blender Extensions listing and the repository's LICENSE.CODE.md.
The Blender Extensions listing for MPFB says its asset packs are CC0 or CC-BY.
A third-party project's license notes state MakeHuman base assets are CC0 1.0; not verified against MakeHuman's own files.
A search snippet reports MPFB2 latest version as 2.0.18 with listed compatibility Blender 4.2 LTS and newer; the snippet's release date (October 10, 2026) comes from a single unverified snippet.
The project's releases page says the preferred install method for MPFB2 is the Blender extension platform.
The MPFB1 plugin (makehuman-plugin-for-blender) is deprecated and replaced by MPFB2.

contradictions: The 2.0.18 version/date snippet and the 4.2 LTS compatibility come from search summaries, not from fetched pages; treat as unconfirmed until checked on the listing.

Asset license: Blender listing says CC0 or CC-BY; a third-party note says CC0 1.0 for MakeHuman base assets. Not a direct contradiction, but the exact per-asset licence needs checking against MakeHuman's own files.
